story.title: OTP multi-factor login for web and mobile banking
story.description: Add a one-time passcode (OTP) step to customer login on web-banking and mobile-banking. The authentication-service generates, sends and verifies six-digit codes with a five-minute expiry; the notification-service delivers each code by SMS to the customer's verified mobile number; customer-db stores the MFA enrolment flag and verified phone number in two new columns. The API gateway exposes new /auth/otp/send and /auth/otp/verify endpoints. Lock the login after five failed codes and record every attempt for audit.
acceptance_criteria: Customers enrolled in MFA must enter a valid six-digit OTP after their password before a session is issued.
Codes expire after five minutes and five failed attempts lock the login for 30 minutes.
OTP SMS messages are delivered within 30 seconds through the notification service.
Every OTP send, success and failure is recorded for audit.

requirement.business_summary: Web and mobile banking customers will be required to complete a one-time passcode (OTP) step after entering their password when they are enrolled in multi-factor authentication. The six-digit code is sent by SMS to the customer's verified mobile number, expires after five minutes, and five failed codes lock the login for 30 minutes. Every OTP send, success and failure is recorded for audit.
requirement.technical_summary: The authentication-service is extended to generate, deliver and verify six-digit OTPs with a five-minute expiry, enforce a five-failed-attempt lockout for 30 minutes, and emit audit records for every send, success and failure. Codes are dispatched as SMS via the notification-service to the customer's verified mobile number. The customer-db adds two columns to hold the MFA enrolment flag and the verified phone number. The api-gateway exposes two new routes, /auth/otp/send and /auth/otp/verify. The web-banking and mobile-banking login flows gain an OTP entry step between password entry and session issuance for MFA-enrolled customers.
requirement.business_domain: Retail Digital Banking — Customer Authentication and Access
affected_capabilities: One-time passcode generation, expiry and verification
Login lockout after repeated failed OTP attempts
Customer MFA enrolment and verified phone number storage
requirement.engineering_scope: Contained change spanning six components: new OTP generation/verification and lockout logic in authentication-service; a new OTP SMS notification in notification-service; two new columns (MFA enrolment flag, verified phone number) in customer-db; two new gateway routes (/auth/otp/send, /auth/otp/verify) in api-gateway; and an OTP entry step in the web-banking and mobile-banking login screens. No changes to balances, payments, cards or loan processing; audit attempt records are written as new entries to the existing append-only audit store without schema change. Thresholds (five-minute expiry, five attempts, 30-minute lockout) are configuration/business rules local to the authentication flow.

tests.title: Security: OTP value is not leaked in audit events
steps: Enroll a test customer in MFA (set enrolment flag and verified phone number).
Trigger an OTP send via /auth/otp/send or login flow.
Retrieve the audit event for the OTP send from audit-db (GET /internal/audit/events filtered by customerId and event type).
Verify the audit event payload does not contain the OTP value.
Repeat for OTP success and failure verification events.
tests.expected: Audit events contain metadata (timestamp, customerId, event type, success/failure flag) but the OTP value is absent or masked.

tests.title: Technical: Customer DB schema includes MFA enrolment flag and verified phone number columns
steps: Query the customer-db schema (e.g., DESCRIBE customer table).
Confirm presence of columns: mfa_enrolled (BOOLEAN, default false) and verified_phone_number (VARCHAR, nullable).
Insert a new customer record without specifying these columns.
Retrieve the record and verify default values: mfa_enrolled = false, verified_phone_number = NULL.
Update the record with a phone number and set mfa_enrolled = true.
Retrieve and verify values persisted correctly.
tests.expected: Schema shows the two columns with correct defaults; updates persist as expected.

tests.title: Compliance: Verified phone number is not returned in customer profile API
steps: Enroll a customer with MFA and set a verified phone number in customer-db.
Authenticate the customer via web/mobile login (including OTP) to obtain a session token.
Call GET /customers/{id} (or equivalent profile endpoint) with the token.
Inspect the response JSON for fields containing the phone number.
Ensure the verified phone number is absent or masked (e.g., not present or only last four digits if any).
tests.expected: The customer profile API does not expose the full verified phone number; PII is protected.

tests.title: Delivery: Notification service logs OTP send attempts for audit
steps: Trigger an OTP send for a test customer via /auth/otp/send.
Query notification-service logs (or audit-db) for an OTP send record.
Verify a log entry exists with customerId, timestamp, and status "sent".
Also verify an audit event is created in audit-db with event type "otp_send".
Repeat for a failed OTP send (e.g., invalid phone number) and verify log indicates failure.
tests.expected: Notification service logs each OTP send attempt; audit-db records an event for each send (success or failure).

tests.title: Operational: OTP failed attempt lockout prevents login for 30 minutes
steps: Enroll a customer in MFA.
Attempt to log in via web or mobile with correct password but incorrect OTP five times consecutively.
After the fifth failure, attempt another login with correct OTP.
Observe login is denied with lockout message.
Wait 30 minutes (or simulate time shift) and retry login with correct OTP.
Observe that login succeeds.
tests.expected: After five failed OTP attempts, account is locked for 30 minutes; subsequent login attempts are rejected until lockout expires.

tests.title: ATM withdrawal functions normally after MFA OTP feature rollout
steps: Ensure an ATM terminal is registered and has sufficient cash.
Using a valid card and PIN, initiate a withdrawal request for an amount within available balance.
Complete the transaction without any OTP prompt.
Verify the transaction completes successfully and the account is debited accordingly.
Verify that no OTP-related audit events are generated for this ATM transaction.
tests.expected: ATM withdrawal proceeds as before; no OTP step is required; audit logs show only standard transaction events.

tests.title: Branch portal login unaffected by web/mobile OTP requirement
steps: A branch staff member logs into the branch portal using username/password (no MFA).
Verify that login succeeds and the user gains access to branch portal functions.
Attempt to log in with invalid credentials; verify appropriate error.
Confirm that no OTP prompt appears during login.
Verify that audit logs for branch portal login do not contain OTP-related events.
tests.expected: Branch portal login works as before, without OTP step; no OTP audit events.

tests.title: Transaction ledger records payments without OTP-related fields
steps: Perform a payment transaction via web or mobile (including OTP step for authentication).
After transaction completion, query the transaction-db for the ledger entry corresponding to the payment.
Inspect the ledger record fields: ensure it contains standard fields (transactionId, amount, timestamp, accounts, etc.) and does not contain any OTP-specific columns (e.g., otp_code, otp_attempt).
Verify that the ledger entry balances (debits = credits) and matches the payment amount.
Ensure that audit-db contains an OTP verification success event linked to the transaction via correlation ID.
tests.expected: Payment ledger entry is unchanged by OTP feature; no OTP fields present; transaction balances correctly.

tests.summary: Selected 15 catalog tests and 8 new tests, covering 14 of 21 impacted nodes (67%); estimated effort is 13.2 hours.

frameworks.reason: PII-bearing components are impacted; the change touches customer data.

findings.text: The change introduces a new authentication step that processes customer identifiers and a verified mobile number, with OTP generation and verification in authentication-service, SMS delivery via notification-service, storage in customer-db, gateway exposure on api-gateway, and login entry points in web-banking and mobile-banking. Review data minimization, purpose limitation and retention for the new OTP artefacts and the verified phone number attribute.

MFA enrolment and phone-number verification touch customer profile and contact flows through customer-service, crm and branch-portal. Confirm the lawful basis and accuracy controls for the verified phone number, and that staff-facing access remains scoped to authorized servicing purposes.

Audit recording of OTP send, success and failure events writes authentication-related personal data to audit-db. Check retention limits, access restrictions and whether audit content captures the OTP value or full destination number in identifiable form.

recommendations: Review data minimization, purpose and retention for OTP and verified-phone data across authentication-service, notification-service, customer-db, api-gateway, web-banking and mobile-banking.
Verify that audit-db authentication event entries do not persist the OTP value, and confirm their retention and access scope.
Confirm that error responses, logs and API contracts for the new api-gateway authentication routes do not expose customer identifiers or phone numbers to unauthorized parties.
Check how data subject access and erasure requests will be handled for the new MFA enrolment flag and verified phone number held in customer-db.

findings.text: The change does not introduce new card data, but it alters the authentication flow at api-gateway, authentication-service and the login steps of mobile-banking and web-banking, which are control points on paths used to reach card-service and atm. Cardholder-data access boundaries around these entry points require re-verification.

Card-data components include card-service, atm, fraud-engine and customer-db. Confirm that OTP handling, notification-service SMS delivery and the two new customer-db columns do not draw cardholder data into non-card scopes or non-card audit paths.

Token validation, session issuance and step-up behaviour in authentication-service feed the api-gateway route that handles card freeze/unfreeze requests to card-service. Check that tokenization, masking and access restrictions on that path remain effective after the authentication change.

recommendations: Confirm that OTP values are not stored, logged or transmitted through card-data handling paths in card-service, atm, fraud-engine and customer-db.
Re-run cardholder-data flow and access tests for api-gateway, mobile-banking, web-banking and authentication-service after the authentication change.
Verify access restrictions, monitoring and audit coverage for authentication-service and notification-service where they sit adjacent to cardholder-data processes.
Check that the new gateway routes follow the same token validation and route policy controls applied to existing card-related routes.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; audit-data components are impacted.

findings.text: Financial-data components account-service, payment-service, transaction-db, loan-service and reporting-db are not changed in business logic, but the new OTP login step gates access to them through web-banking, mobile-banking and api-gateway. Assess whether transaction authorization and segregation of duties could be affected by the modified session issuance path.

audit-db receives new authentication event entries on the existing append-only store without schema change. Verify that records for access to financial processing remain complete, immutable and within the approved retention period.

The customer-db schema change adds MFA enrolment and verified phone columns. Assess change-management and reconciliation impacts on downstream financial data consumers such as risk-engine and fraud-engine that rely on customer-linked records.

recommendations: Obtain control-owner approval and evidence of financial and schema change testing for api-gateway, authentication-service, customer-db, audit-db, web-banking and mobile-banking.
Verify that audit-db authentication event records remain complete, immutable and retained in line with policy for financial-process access.
Confirm that OTP expiry, attempt and lockout thresholds are configuration-controlled and changed only through approved change procedures.
Document how the new customer-db columns will be reflected in reconciliation and downstream reporting checks.

frameworks.reason: directly changed components have criticality >= 8; the authentication flow changes.

findings.text: Directly changed components api-gateway, authentication-service, customer-db, notification-service, web-banking and mobile-banking carry tier1 or tier2 criticality. Service-owner approval, dependency review and a tested rollback plan are expected before release.

The change alters the authentication flow and the external API contract through two new api-gateway routes, and modifies the customer-db schema. Architecture, security and data governance review records for these touchpoints require confirmation.

Operational readiness: monitoring, alerting and support runbooks for OTP delivery failures across notification-service and authentication-service, including dependency on audit-db for event capture, need verification before go-live.

recommendations: Record service-owner change approval and the rollback plan for api-gateway, authentication-service, customer-db, notification-service, web-banking and mobile-banking.
Verify authorization tests, operational monitoring and release evidence for the new OTP routes in api-gateway and authentication-service.
Confirm schema-change review and data-owner sign-off for the two new customer-db columns.
Check that notification-service SMS delivery changes and authentication-service lockout logic have documented runbooks and alert thresholds.
